Kaplan-Meier survival and recurrence

Source: R/kmr.R
kmrec.Rd

Estimates the share still without an event at each time since the start (release, placement, a case opening, the last incident at a place) by Kaplan-Meier, by group, with Greenwood's standard error and the log-scale interval of survival::survfit() (its default), each group's median (where the curve sits at exactly 1/2, halfway to its next fall, as survfit() does), and the log-rank test between groups (survival::survdiff()). Each product step is a factor in \([0, 1]\), so the curve starts at most 1 and never rises (proof("kmrec")).

Usage

kmrec(time, event = NULL, grp = NULL, unit = NULL, end = NULL, level = 0.95)

Arguments

time

Durations from 0, or with unit the times of events: finite numbers from 0.

event

NULL (every duration ends in an event) or 1 for an event and 0 for a censored duration (logical or numbers); not read with unit.

grp

NULL, or the group of each time: labels. With unit it must be the same for every time of a unit.

unit

NULL, or the unit of each event time: labels.

end

With unit, NULL or the end of observation: one number at or after every time.

level

The confidence level: one number strictly between 0 and 1.

Value

An object of class kmrec, a list: km, one row per group and distinct time (grp, time, nrisk, nevent, ncens, surv, se, lo, hi); med, one row per group (grp, n, events, median, NA when the curve never reaches 1/2); lr, NULL for one group, otherwise the log-rank stat, df and p; n, the durations; and level.

Details

Durations are given directly (time, with event 0 where a duration was cut short), or, with unit, time holds the times of events and the durations are the gaps between one unit's consecutive events (time to a repeat incident at a place, a repeat admission of a person); with end each unit's last gap, from its last event to end, enters as censored, so units with long quiet spells count.

References

Kaplan, E. L. and Meier, P. (1958). Nonparametric estimation from incomplete observations. Journal of the American Statistical Association, 53(282), 457-481. doi:10.1080/01621459.1958.10501452

Maltz, M. D. (1984). Recidivism. Academic Press.

Examples

kmrec(c(3, 8, 8, 12, 20, 24), event = c(1, 1, 0, 1, 0, 1),
      grp = c("a", "a", "a", "b", "b", "b"))
#> kmrec: 6 durations
#>  grp n events median
#>    a 3      2      8
#>    b 3      2     24
#> log-rank chi-square 2.469388 on 1 df, p 0.1160831
# repeat incidents at three places, watched to day 100
kmrec(c(2, 9, 30, 5, 70, 11, 12, 13),
      unit = rep(c("p", "q", "r"), c(3, 2, 3)), end = 100)$med
#>   grp n events median
#> 1 all 8      5     43
